Commentary.Commentary: Back to the drawing board - After putting up a decent fight in the first ODI, Afghanistan crumbled with the ball in the 2nd ODI and even after a very good start with the bat, the pressure of chasing 403 simply got to them and they ended up losing the game by 170 runs. They will be eager to tweak the bowling and look to contain the Indian batters a bit more through the middle phase, but it will be a big challenge against a team that's riding high on confidence. Righto, will we see some sort of a turnaround and probably an upset today? Or will India simply carry on their merry way? Only time will tell. There's also a forecast of rain in the afternoon, which might delay things a bit, but the weather is expected to clear after that, so we should get a full game in. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

Expect some changes - With India having already sealed the three-match series 2-0, they will look to test their bench strength, and someone like Harshit Rana, who is coming back from injury, could get a go in this game. Overall, the hosts have immaculate depth in all areas of the game and they will be eager to clean sweep the series.

One final bout - Hello, and welcome to our coverage of the 3rd ODI between India and Afghanistan, set to be played at the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. This is the final match of Afghanistan's tour to India, and so far the hosts have bossed proceedings and will be eyeing up a clean sweep. Afghanistan, on the other hand, will be hoping to step up after how they got demolished in the 2nd ODI and look to end the tour with a 'W' against their name.

The Chennai assignment - From Chandigarh to the Dhauladhar up north, and then rolling through the plains of Lucknow, this Afghanistan tour of India is all set to conclude down south in the Detroit of India. The series lays down its final tent at the MA Chidambaram Stadium for the third and final ODI. India have clinched the series handsomely and are eyeing a clean sweep. Afghanistan, still trying to firm their footing in the format and proving their credentials against the ‘big boys’, will be aiming to salvage pride and bow out with a zillion learnings. A fort that rarely falls - Now here is a little something worth chewing on. This is India's first home ODI series since the New Zealand nightmare back in January. That series stung. It broke records, but more than that, it put a dent in something India hold very, very dear, which is their stranglehold on home soil. Because look, in 25 home bilateral series since 2013, India have lost just four of those. The Kiwis managed it once earlier this year. The Aussies pulled it off twice, in 2019 and 2023. The Proteas did it once as well, in 2015. That is the company you need to be in to beat India at home. Afghanistan are not at that level yet, and the series scoreline reflects that. India have been commanding, handing the visitors one of their biggest ODI defeats. But Afghanistan arrived here in fine form, having won five consecutive ODI series before this one, including defeating the heavyweights South Africa in 2024. So they are definitely a side to beat on their given day. This tour, however, has simply been their toughest examination in the format yet. A real trial by fire. But they would hope that they bow out with a collective performance and avoid a whitewash. Firing on all cylinders - That’s Indian batting and bowling units for you. Batting-wise, they have just been simply ruthless. They smashed 402 runs in the second ODI, thanks to twin-centurions, Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan. Both these blokes are having a stellar run in 2026. Of course, they scored the bulk of runs in the IPL, but since the last ODI World Cup, Gill has been India’s third-best run getter, after Rohit and Kohli, whereas Kishan, having played just two ODIs in this span and coming back after a prolonged absence, has an average of 79.5. But here is where India will have a small word with themselves. Despite those mammoth contributions at the top, the middle order has not quite fired in this series. KL Rahul has looked decent enough, but Shreyas Iyer, who is very much a fixture in this ODI setup now, has not had the returns to match that status. In 2026, Iyer averages just 19.6, with 98 runs in five ODI innings. For a batter of his calibre, that is a number he will want to fix, and Chennai is as good a place as any to start. The return of Rana - Into an already ruthless bowling lineup with a commendable depth of personnel comes Harshit Rana, added to India's squad for the series finale in Chennai. A knee injury ruled him out of the T20 World Cup earlier this year, also missing the entire IPL along the way. After undergoing surgery and completing his rehab at the BCCI Centre of Excellence, Rana has linked up with the squad in Chennai, providing the team management with an additional high-pace weapon to partner alongside Arshdeep Singh, who led the pace attack in the second match, with a clinical three-wicket haul. And then there are the two youngsters who have made this series their own. Gurnoor Brar has been outstanding, picking up three wickets in both Dharamsala and Lucknow, bowling with excellent control and extracting steep bounce that his tall frame generates almost naturally. Prince Yadav, on his maiden national call-up after a strong IPL 2026 campaign, has been equally eye-catching with his raw pace and hard-length bowling in the second ODI. What's beyond Gurbaz? Rahmanullah Gurbaz has been Afghanistan's brightest spark in this series. A hundred in the first game, a brisk 41 off 33 in the second. He has led from the front every time. Since the last ODI World Cup, he has been Afghanistan’s leading run getter, with four hundreds and three fifties. The challenge now is to build a more collective batting effort around him. Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmat Shah have shown decent touches in this series, and young Sediqullah Atal is soaking in every experience that comes his way. The ingredients are there. It simply comes down to doing it more consistently, and a series like this will only help them massively. The form of captain Hashmatullah Shahidi has been under the scanner of late, though. Averaging 26.25 since the last global tournament, he has struggled for both consistency and fluency in the middle order. And with just 31 runs this series, a good stint in Chennai would go a long way, both for his own confidence and for what Afghanistan need from their skipper in the middle overs. A big challenge for the young bowling attack - Defensively, Afghanistan's greatest strength lies in their spin-bowling department. Rashid Khan remains the jewel in the crown, having claimed three-for in Lucknow, and alongside him, the emergence of Nangeyalia Kharote has added a fresh and exciting dimension to their attack. Young off-spinner AM Ghazanfar completes what is a genuinely threatening spin trio, one that will fancy their chances of putting the Indian middle order under some pressure. With the pace ball, options are a little thinner after an injury to Omarzai. 22-year-old Bilal Sami had a tough outing in Lucknow, going for 90 runs in his spell of just 8.5 overs, and will be looking to make amends. Mohammad Saleem, another emerging young pacer, who impressed in the Tests on this very tour, offers a more promising case and will be hoping to carry that form into the white-ball arena. Team form (Last 5 completed ODIs, recent first) - IND - WWLLW | AFG - LLWWW. What to expect? Chepauk and spin. The two have gone hand in hand for as long as anyone can remember. But the numbers tell a slightly different story these days. Since the start of 2023, pacers have actually outbowled the spinners at this ground in ODIs, picking up 51 wickets to spinners' 36 across six matches, including the 2023 ODI World Cup. The surface has changed its character, and the bowlers who have adapted have reaped the rewards. That said, writing off spin at Chepauk would be a brave call. It is still very much in the game and the teams would closely read the conditions before. So expect a gripping contest at Chepauk, where ODI returns after almost three years.
